mutants.name: checked_in_the_handler_only
mutants.why: adds a 404 check in the HTTP handler but leaves Runner.decide on the owner connection, so a direct call with the wrong workspace still records the decision.

mutants.name: existence_checked_as_owner
mutants.why: checks that the run exists on the owner connection, so another workspace's run is found and the caller gets 409, not 404.

mutants.name: nothing_pending_is_404
mutants.why: maps every refusal to 404, so the owner deciding a step with nothing pending no longer gets 409.

mutants.name: tenant_without_404
mutants.why: switches back to the tenant connection but another workspace's run (and an unknown run) still answers 409 instead of 404 "no such run".

unmergeable.name: owner_connection_with_where_clause
unmergeable.why: behaves correctly but keeps a request-path query on db.owner() and relies on hand-written workspace_id filters, which AGENTS.md rule 1 forbids (row-level security must do the isolating).
judge_blocking: Runner.decide, which the approve/reject HTTP handler calls, still queries workspace tables (agent_runs, run_steps) through db.owner(), which bypasses row-level security. AGENTS.md forbids this on the request path. The fix relies on hand-written workspace_id WHERE clauses instead of db.tenant(workspace_id), so tenant isolation rests on query text and not on RLS. The new docstring also wrongly says RLS hides other workspaces' runs.

mutants.name: estimated_tokens
mutants.why: recomputes the cost from token estimates instead of the provider-reported tokens, so hits are still billed from an estimate.

mutants.name: request_actual_cost
mutants.why: stores the request's total actual cost, which includes the escalated cheap first try, so a later hit is billed for calls that did not produce the answer.

mutants.name: routed_primary_prices
mutants.why: prices the answer with the routed primary model, which is wrong after a fallback answered instead.

unmergeable.name: hard_coded_cache_share
unmergeable.why: fixes the stored cost but replaces the catalogue's cache.cached_answer_charge with a hard-coded 0.10 in the ledger, so a price change in models.yaml would silently stop applying to cache hits.
judge_blocking: `record_cache_hit` in `src/mrp/ledger.py` hard-codes `Decimal("0.10")` in place of the catalogue's `cache.cached_answer_charge`. The charge belongs in configuration, so changing the catalogue value would no longer change what cache hits are billed.

mutants.name: error_event_then_fallback
mutants.why: sends the provider_error event but keeps going, so the fallback model's answer is still spliced in after it.

mutants.name: no_fallback_in_streams
mutants.why: stops on any streaming failure, so a model that fails before its first chunk is no longer replaced by the fallback.

mutants.name: second_error_event
mutants.why: restores the guard but still sends a no_provider error after the provider_error event, so the stream does not end with the one provider_error the brief asks for.

mutants.name: stops_without_the_error_event
mutants.why: stops before the fallback but sends no error event, so the client cannot tell the answer was cut off.

mutants.name: all_time_spend
mutants.why: sums billed amounts over all time, so earlier months count against this month's budget.

mutants.name: budget_read_as_owner
mutants.why: reads the budget on the owner connection, so a workspace sees another workspace's budget and everyone's spend.

mutants.name: estimate_added_to_spend
mutants.why: adds the request's estimated cost to what was billed, so a request is refused while the month is still below the budget (estimates are never spend).

mutants.name: provider_cost_not_bill
mutants.why: compares our provider cost (actual_cost) instead of what the customer was billed, so spend including markup can exceed the budget unnoticed.

mutants.name: refused_only_above_the_limit
mutants.why: refuses only when spend is strictly above the limit, so a month whose bill has exactly reached the budget keeps being answered.

unmergeable.name: budget_as_float
unmergeable.why: stores and compares the budget as a float (double precision column, float model field), which AGENTS.md forbids for money (Decimal, 8 places, half up).
judge_blocking: The budget is handled as float instead of Decimal, which AGENTS.md forbids for money. `BudgetIn.monthly_limit` is a float, the `mrp.budgets.monthly_limit` column is `double precision`, and `check_entitlements` compares `float(spent)` against it. This can give wrong results at the boundary, and `GET` can return values that are not the exact 8-place amount the user set.

mutants.name: approvals_ignore_cancellation
mutants.why: approving or rejecting a step of a cancelled run is still accepted and re-queues the run.

mutants.name: cancelled_as_owner
mutants.why: cancels on the owner connection, so another workspace can cancel a run it does not own.

mutants.name: ended_runs_cancelled_too
mutants.why: lets a run that has already succeeded or been rejected be cancelled instead of answering 409.

mutants.name: status_set_but_worker_never_checks
mutants.why: the endpoint marks the run cancelled but the worker never looks again, so a running run executes its remaining steps (and ends as succeeded).

mutants.name: listing_includes_the_hash
mutants.why: the listing also returns key_hash, so items have more than the four fields and leak the stored hash.

mutants.name: own_key_hash_includes_bearer
mutants.why: hashes the whole Authorization header (with "Bearer "), so the key in use is never recognised and can revoke itself.

mutants.name: revoke_deletes_the_row
mutants.why: deletes the key instead of setting revoked_at, so a revoked key disappears from the listing.

mutants.name: revoked_as_owner
mutants.why: revokes on the owner connection, so one workspace can revoke another workspace's key.

unmergeable.name: logs_the_new_key
unmergeable.why: writes the newly created API key into a log line and relies on the redaction filter to scrub it; AGENTS.md rule 3 says keys are never logged, the filter is only a second line of defence.
judge_blocking: create_api_key passes the plaintext new API key to log.info (key=%s), relying on the redaction filter to scrub it. AGENTS.md and the task both say a key must never appear in a log line, so the key must not be passed to the logger at all.
